title: Autonomy score metric: landed output tokens per human-typed token
summary: Defined the autonomy score as output tokens of sessions whose work merged to git main ÷ genuinely human-typed input tokens (excluding tool results, hooks, system reminders, scheduled-task and judge/onboarding prompts). First measurement (2026-06-10, 10:00–15:00 block): ~1.2K human tokens steered 1.26M output tokens (~1,000× amplification); 268K (21%) of output belonged to sessions whose work landed on main → autonomy score ≈ 220×. Merged artifact itself was +724 lines ≈ 9K tokens → 0.7% raw yield (output-to-merged-code refinement ratio). Caveats: session-level attribution is coarse, and merged-to-main undercounts non-code outputs (research, graph wiring, decisions). Measurement method: parse transcript JSONLs in ~/.claude/projects, sum message.usage.output_tokens per session, match sessions to merged commits by branch/commit keywords.
